stem: The student wants to introduce the Orlenka Viaduct to an audience unfamiliar with it. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Orlenka Viaduct is a curved concrete railway bridge.
• It carries a freight line across the Tesna River valley.
• It was completed in 1974.
• Its longest span measures 212 meters.
• In 2019, engineers added sensors to its piers to monitor vibration.
choices: Completed in 1974, the Orlenka Viaduct had vibration sensors added to its piers in 2019.
The Orlenka Viaduct, a curved concrete railway bridge, carries freight trains across the Tesna River valley.
The Orlenka Viaduct's longest span, at 212 meters, was a remarkable length for a bridge built in 1974.
In 2019, engineers began monitoring vibration in the piers of the Orlenka Viaduct, which opened in 1974.
explanation: A reader who has never heard of the Orlenka Viaduct first needs to know what it is and what it does. Choice B gives it a category label in an appositive ("a curved concrete railway bridge") and then states its purpose (carrying freight trains across the Tesna River valley). After reading it, a newcomer knows what the viaduct is.

A.why: You picked a sentence built from two dates. It tells the reader when the viaduct was finished and when it got sensors, but it never says that the viaduct is a bridge. A reader new to the topic still doesn't know what the Orlenka Viaduct is.

C.why: The notes give the span length but never say it was remarkable for its time, so that judgment goes beyond the evidence. The sentence also skips what the viaduct is, which an unfamiliar audience needs first.

D.why: You went for a later development, the 2019 vibration monitoring. The sentence treats the viaduct as something the reader already knows and never says that it is a railway bridge or what it carries.

stem: The student wants to introduce the Open Corners program to an audience unfamiliar with it. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Open Corners is a municipal initiative in the city of Bramhall.
• It converts unused corner parking spaces into small public seating areas.
• The program began in 2016 with four sites.
• By 2023, it had expanded to 61 sites.
• A spin-off program, Open Alleys, adds lighting and plantings to service alleys.
choices: Open Alleys, a spin-off of the Open Corners program, adds lighting and plantings to Bramhall's service alleys.
The Open Corners program in Bramhall grew from just four sites in 2016 to a total of 61 sites by 2023.
Open Corners is a Bramhall city initiative that converts unused corner parking spaces into public seating areas.
Since 2016, Open Corners has become the most popular public-space initiative in the history of Bramhall.
explanation: An unfamiliar audience needs to learn what Open Corners is and what it does. Choice C labels it ("a Bramhall city initiative") and states its purpose (turning unused corner parking spaces into public seating). That is the basic identifying information a newcomer needs.

A.why: This is the classic trap for this question type. The sentence is about the offshoot program, Open Alleys, and mentions Open Corners only in passing. It never says what Open Corners itself does.

B.why: You chose the program's growth figures. The numbers are accurate, but a reader who has never heard of Open Corners still wouldn't know what those 61 sites are.

D.why: The notes never compare Open Corners with other initiatives or call it the most popular. That claim isn't supported, and the sentence also never explains what the program does.

stem: The student wants to introduce the lantern wrasse to an audience unfamiliar with it. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The lantern wrasse (Thalassoma lucerna) is a small reef fish.
• It removes parasites from the skin of larger fish.
• It lives in shallow waters off the coast of West Africa.
• Scientists first described the species in 1931.
• During the breeding season, males develop a bright orange stripe.
choices: First described by scientists in 1931, Thalassoma lucerna is commonly known as the lantern wrasse.
During the breeding season, male lantern wrasses develop a bright orange stripe along their bodies.
Lantern wrasses remove parasites from larger fish, which could not survive on the reef without them.
The lantern wrasse, a small reef fish found off West Africa, removes parasites from larger fish.
explanation: Choice D tells a newcomer what the lantern wrasse is ("a small reef fish found off West Africa") and what it does (removes parasites from larger fish). The category label, placed right after the name, is what an unfamiliar audience needs.

A.why: You picked the sentence with the scientific name and the discovery date. It never says that the lantern wrasse is a fish or what it does, so a new reader learns only a name and a year.

B.why: You chose a secondary detail, the males' breeding coloration. The sentence assumes the reader already knows what a lantern wrasse is and never identifies it as a reef fish.

C.why: The notes never say that larger fish depend on lantern wrasses to survive, so that claim goes beyond the evidence. The sentence also leaves out what kind of animal the lantern wrasse is.

stem: The student wants to introduce the Kestrel Survey Telescope to an audience unfamiliar with it. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Kestrel Survey Telescope is a ground-based optical telescope.
• It photographs the entire visible night sky every three nights.
• It is located on Cerro Varela in northern Chile.
• Construction of the telescope began in 2018.
• Its camera contains 1.2 billion pixels.
choices: The Kestrel Survey Telescope, a ground-based optical telescope, photographs the entire visible night sky every three nights.
The camera of the Kestrel Survey Telescope, located on Cerro Varela in northern Chile, contains 1.2 billion pixels.
The Kestrel's camera contains 1.2 billion pixels, more than the camera of any other telescope in the world.
Cerro Varela, a mountain in northern Chile, is where construction of the Kestrel Survey Telescope began in 2018.
explanation: Choice A names the Kestrel Survey Telescope, says what type of instrument it is ("a ground-based optical telescope"), and states its job (photographing the whole visible night sky every three nights). A reader new to the topic learns both what it is and what it does.

B.why: You chose a sentence about one piece of equipment and the telescope's location. It never says what kind of telescope the Kestrel is or what it is used for.

C.why: The notes give the pixel count but never compare it with other telescopes, so "more than any other" isn't supported. The sentence also uses the short name "the Kestrel" as if the reader already knew what it was.

D.why: You went for the site and the construction date. The sentence is mostly about the mountain and never tells an unfamiliar reader what the telescope does.

stem: The student wants to introduce the Laskey Shuttle Test to an audience unfamiliar with it. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Laskey Shuttle Test is a fitness assessment.
• It measures an athlete's ability to repeat short sprints with little rest.
• Athletes run six 20-meter sprints, separated by 15 seconds of rest.
• Physiologist Mara Laskey developed the test in 2004.
• A version adapted for wheelchair athletes was introduced in 2015.
choices: In 2015, a version of the Laskey Shuttle Test was introduced that had been adapted for wheelchair athletes.
The Laskey Shuttle Test is a fitness assessment that measures how well athletes repeat short sprints with little rest.
Physiologist Mara Laskey developed her shuttle test in 2004, and it is now the standard test in team sports.
In the Laskey Shuttle Test, athletes run six 20-meter sprints, each one separated by 15 seconds of rest.
explanation: Choice B identifies the Laskey Shuttle Test as a fitness assessment and states its purpose: measuring how well athletes repeat short sprints with little rest. Someone who has never heard of the test now knows what it is and what it is for.

A.why: This is the subtype's trap. It reports a later spin-off, the wheelchair version, and assumes the reader already knows what the original test is.

C.why: The notes never say the test became the standard in team sports, so that claim goes beyond the evidence. The sentence also never says what the test measures.

D.why: You picked the procedure. It describes the sprints but never says that this is a fitness assessment or what it is meant to measure, so a new reader doesn't know why anyone runs it.

stem: Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Jacquard loom was first demonstrated in France in 1804.
• It is a weaving machine that uses punched cards to control which threads are raised.
• This allowed complex patterns such as brocade to be woven automatically.
• Its punched cards later influenced Charles Babbage's designs for calculating machines.
The student wants to introduce the Jacquard loom to an audience unfamiliar with it.
choices: The punched cards of the Jacquard loom later influenced Charles Babbage's designs for calculating machines.
The Jacquard loom, first demonstrated in France in 1804, is a weaving machine controlled by punched cards.
The Jacquard loom, the first machine ever to use punched cards, was demonstrated in France in 1804.
In 1804, France saw the first demonstration of the Jacquard loom, which later influenced Charles Babbage.
explanation: A reader who has never heard of the Jacquard loom first needs to know what it is. Choice B attaches the label "a weaving machine" to the name and says how it works (punched cards), so a newcomer knows what the loom is.

A.why: You picked a later development. This choice describes the loom's influence on Babbage without ever saying that the loom is a weaving machine, so it assumes the reader already knows what it is.

C.why: The notes never say the loom was the first machine ever to use punched cards. This choice claims more than the notes support, and it still doesn't say what the loom does.

D.why: You were drawn to the date and the Babbage connection. This choice names the loom but never explains that it is a machine for weaving, so the unfamiliar reader is left guessing.

stem: Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The glycemic index (GI) was developed in 1981 by researchers at the University of Toronto.
• The GI is a scale that ranks carbohydrate foods by how quickly they raise blood sugar.
• Pure glucose is assigned a value of 100.
• A related measure, glycemic load, was later proposed to account for portion size as well.
The student wants to introduce the glycemic index to an audience unfamiliar with it.
choices: Glycemic load, a measure proposed after the glycemic index, also accounts for portion size.
On the glycemic index, developed in 1981, pure glucose is assigned a value of 100.
The glycemic index, developed in 1981, is a scale that ranks carbohydrate foods by portion size.
The glycemic index is a scale that ranks carbohydrate foods by how quickly they raise blood sugar.
explanation: A newcomer needs to know what the glycemic index is and what it measures. Choice D labels it "a scale" and states its purpose, which is ranking carbohydrate foods by how quickly they raise blood sugar.

A.why: You landed on the spin-off measure. This choice is about glycemic load and never explains what the glycemic index itself is.

B.why: This choice gives a detail of the scale (glucose = 100) but assumes the reader already knows what the glycemic index measures. Without that, "a value of 100" means nothing to them.

C.why: According to the notes, the GI ranks foods by how quickly they raise blood sugar. Portion size is what glycemic load adds, so this choice gets the GI's purpose wrong.

stem: Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Glossopteris is an extinct genus of seed-bearing plants.
• It flourished about 299 to 252 million years ago.
• Its fossils have been found in South America, Africa, India, Antarctica, and Australia.
• Its name comes from the Greek word for "tongue," after the shape of its leaves.
The student wants to introduce Glossopteris to an audience unfamiliar with it.
choices: Glossopteris, an extinct genus of seed-bearing plants, flourished about 299 to 252 million years ago.
Fossils of Glossopteris have been found in South America, Africa, India, Antarctica, and Australia.
The name Glossopteris comes from the Greek word for "tongue," after the shape of its leaves.
Glossopteris, a seed-bearing plant still growing in Antarctica, has leaves shaped like a tongue.
explanation: A reader who has never heard of Glossopteris needs to know what kind of thing it is. Choice A uses an appositive, "an extinct genus of seed-bearing plants," to label it, then places it in time.

B.why: You went for the most striking fact. This choice lists where the fossils were found but never says Glossopteris is a plant, so it treats the reader as already informed.

C.why: This choice explains how Glossopteris got its name, which is a secondary detail. It never says the name belongs to an extinct plant.

D.why: The notes say Glossopteris is extinct. Only its fossils turn up in Antarctica, so "still growing" contradicts the notes.

stem: Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Tok Pisin is a creole language spoken in Papua New Guinea.
• Most of its vocabulary comes from English.
• Its name means "talk pidgin."
• Its word save, meaning "to know," comes from Portuguese.
The student wants to introduce Tok Pisin to an audience unfamiliar with it.
choices: In Tok Pisin, the word save, which means "to know," was borrowed from Portuguese.
Tok Pisin, a creole language spoken in Papua New Guinea, drawing most of its vocabulary from English.
Tok Pisin, a creole language spoken in Papua New Guinea, draws most of its vocabulary from English.
The name Tok Pisin, which is spoken in Papua New Guinea, means "talk pidgin."
explanation: Choice C labels Tok Pisin "a creole language," says where it is spoken, and adds where its words come from. It is a complete sentence that tells a newcomer exactly what Tok Pisin is.

A.why: This choice focuses on one borrowed word and assumes the reader already knows Tok Pisin is a language. It is a detail for an informed reader.

B.why: The content is right, but "drawing" is not a main verb, so the sentence is a fragment. You need the conjugated verb "draws."

D.why: You picked the note about the name. This choice explains what "Tok Pisin" means without saying it is a language, so it never identifies the subject.

stem: Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
stimulus:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• A derecho is a widespread, long-lived windstorm produced by a fast-moving band of thunderstorms.
• The term was coined in 1888 by physicist Gustavus Hinrichs.
• It comes from a Spanish word meaning "straight."
• In 2020, a derecho flattened crops across Iowa.
The student wants to introduce derechos to an audience unfamiliar with them.
choices: The term derecho, from a Spanish word for "straight," was coined in 1888 by Gustavus Hinrichs.
A derecho is a widespread, long-lived windstorm produced by a fast-moving band of thunderstorms.
In 2020, a derecho flattened crops across Iowa, more than a century after the term was coined.
Derecho comes from a Spanish word meaning "straight"; however, it was coined by Gustavus Hinrichs.
explanation: An unfamiliar reader first needs a definition. Choice B gives the category, "a windstorm," and explains what produces it, so the reader knows what a derecho is.

A.why: You went for the history of the word. This choice explains who coined "derecho" and where the word comes from, but never says that a derecho is a storm.

C.why: This choice describes one derecho's damage and assumes the reader already knows what a derecho is. It works as an example, not as an introduction.

D.why: "However" signals a contrast, but a Spanish origin and an English-speaking coiner don't conflict. Even with a different transition, this choice never says what a derecho is.
